name: Robert M. Potts Landscape Design & Construction
founded: Houzz bio: serving Los Altos since 1945 · Yelp: "Established" client relationships of 17+ years
audience: Los Altos, Los Altos Hills, Atherton properties
description: Design-build landscape practice: flagstone patios, interlocking pavers, brick and cement walkways, garden lighting, decks, arbors, irrigation, lawns, and waterfalls/rock work. 80-year lineage per Houzz profile.
serviceCopy: Drawn and built by one practice.
Hardscape detailed to drain properly, first time.
Water features and rock work set by eye.
Planting that reads well in year ten.
insight: Reviews describe pool-side waterfalls, driveway rebuilds and 17-year client relationships — the kind of proof a $10K site monetises.
usps: Eight-decade practice name in Los Altos
Designer and builder in one head (no hand-off losses)
differentiators: The only boutique with a lineage story and a garden of real work; zero published evidence
persona: The last old-school design-build firm on the Avenue

reputation.note: Tiny review count, extraordinary depth of client relationships — reputation is entirely referral-based.

afford: A firm claiming a 1945 lineage has a broken URL as its only web presence
Houzz profile with one project entry: nothing working for them
Old-money referral clientele needs a polished front door to justify premium fees
risk: Aged principal — must be a "we update it for you" engagement
Low digital literacy: keep scope tight and self-updating minimal

art.logo: Draw an estate-style monogram (RMP) with a leaf-line
art.photoNote: Requires a commissioned shoot: 10–14 projects, plan drawings, plant details

copy.h1: A landscape practice older than Silicon Valley, with a website that no longer loads.
copy.sub: Design-build gardens: hardscape, water, mature planting, lighting — by the same hand from first drawing to last stone.
copy.lede: Robert M. Potts has been designing and building Los Altos gardens for longer than any firm in the valley. The web address people find on Houzz leads nowhere. That is the entire gap.

concept.dir: Botanical drawing-plate system: plan-line illustrations, archival "since 1945" ribbon, project plates with elevation details, slow parallax.
interactive: Project plate index with hover detail
concept.threeD: Discreet three.js terrain model that rotates on scroll for the process section (drainage/massing read) — lazy-loaded, optional, low-poly.
concept.refs: A landscape architect's monograph, not a lawn-care page.

web.note: Houzz lists www.pottslandscape.com/ as the business site, but the domain does not serve a site: fetching it lands on a Google Maps place page, and the Google Business Profile shows "Add website" (empty). YellowPages record shows "Add Website" too. So: an advertised URL that no longer works = no functional web presence.
